transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump is in Shenzhen, China, meeting with leaders of other nations at the APEC
summit.
That's included Mexico and Canada's leaders.
Later, he's expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin in
a highly anticipated conversation.
Trump said Putin will want to talk about ending the war in Ukraine on his terms.
Former U.S. Ambassador to China Nicholas Burns says this is unfortunate because Ukrainian
President Volodymyr Zelensky is not at the table with the other three leaders.
This meeting looks somewhat like the Yalta meeting, February 1945, Stalin, FDR, Churchill
deciding the fate of Eastern Europe over the heads of the Eastern Europeans.
There are a lot of differences between 81 years ago and now.
But the fact that three very strong countries in the world will be discussing what should
happen in Ukraine when Putin's the aggressor and Zelensky's the victim, I think is a major
problem for U.S. credibility in the NATO alliance, certainly, and also with the Ukrainians.
He spoke to NPR's morning edition.
Chinese leader Xi Jinping has called for free and open trade.
This comes after the Trump administration has further restricted China's access to advanced
artificial intelligence chips.
Same with Cynthia's Jennifer Pack reports from Shenzhen, China.
Xi says trade and investment barriers should be eliminated without naming the U.S.
He was speaking at an Asia-Pacific summit where many participating countries have been
hit with U.S. tariffs and export controls.
This week the U.S. Commerce Department started blocking the remote access of top U.S. chips
from the likes of Nvidia.
This will affect Chinese AI firms on the cutting edge.
The Chinese Commerce Ministry has objected to this, saying the U.S. has abused export
controls and overstretched the concept of national security.
Xi has a chance to bring the issue up with President Trump when they meet.
Jennifer Pack, NPR News, Shenzhen.
Stocks opened mixed this morning as computer chip giant Nvidia reported better than expected
financial results.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the Dow Jones industrial average slipped about 250 points
in early trading.
Nvidia says its sales doubled in the most recent quarter compared to a year ago, easily
topping forecasters' expectations.
The chipmaker's earnings call on Tuesday was led by Interim CEO Colette Kress.
She stepped in after the company's embattled co-founder Jensen Wong resigned last week.
Target stores just reported their strongest sales growth in almost five years.
The discount retailer also raised its outlook for business in the coming year.
Home builders broke ground on more houses in October than the previous month, but permits
for future construction were down.
Their confidence has been hammered by high mortgage rates, rising material costs and
a shortage of construction workers.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
On Wall Street, the Dow is now down about 380 points.
This is NPR.
California officials have blocked the self-driving Waymo cars from operating on state highways.
Now Waymo has decided to suspend its operations on all freeways across the country.
There are concerns about safety.
California officials say that recently three Waymo vehicles drove into an active construction
zone on a part of a closed California freeway.
Globally, Muslims are expected to outnumber Christians by the year 2035.
NPR's Jason D. Rose reports that is among the findings of a new study on religious trends
from Pew Research.
Pew projects that by the year 2070, Christians will decline to less than half of the U.S.
population, though they'll remain the country's largest single religious group.
At the same time, religiously unaffiliated people will rise to just over 40%, mostly
due to people leaving Christianity.
Currently, Judaism is the largest non-Christian religion in the U.S., but researchers say that
by 2070, Jews will be outnumbered by both Muslims and Hindus in this country if recent
demographic trends continue.
Globally, Pew projects that more than half of the world's Christians will live in sub-Saharan
Africa by the year 2070, largely due to higher birth rates there.
Jason D. Rose, NPR News.
After what feels like forever, at least for fans, the video game Grand Theft Auto 6 launches
tomorrow.
It's been a 13-year wait, actually, for the latest installment of one of the most popular
video games ever created.
Players in New Zealand will get the first opportunity to play.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Trump attends APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, ahead of planned Xi and Putin meeting
Former Ambassador Nicholas Burns criticizes Trump-Xi-Putin talks on Ukraine excluding Zelensky
Xi Jinping calls for free trade at APEC as US restricts China's access to AI chips
Stocks open mixed as Nvidia reports sales doubling; Dow slips about 250 points
Target posts strongest sales growth in nearly five years and raises outlook
October housing starts rise while building permits for future construction fall
California blocks Waymo self-driving cars from state highways after construction zone incidents
Pew study projects Muslims will outnumber Christians globally by 2035
Grand Theft Auto 6 set to launch tomorrow after 13-year wait
